note: Updated Thu 8 Oct 2026, run before Asia's open; one normal session since Wednesday 7 Oct's close. Wednesday US close: S&P 500 7,801.77 (-0.22%), Nasdaq Composite 27,538.69 (-0.22%), Dow 51,179.87 (-0.66%), Russell 2000 2,793.20 (-1.31%, lagging on rate sensitivity), VIX 15.08 (+0.47%). Gold/silver sold off: GLD-equivalent gold future $4,131.20 (-1.34%), silver future $60.01 (-1.90%), with silver miners GDX/SLVP/SILJ all down 3-5%. The key new inputs since Tuesday's run: FOMC minutes from the Sept 15-16 meeting released Oct 7-8 confirmed a 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% under new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh (12-0) with a hawkish dot plot; the 10-year Treasury yield spiked to a 24-year high near 5.33-5.36% before easing slightly after a well-received 10-year auction; and a research pass corrected a stale 'ongoing government shutdown' assumption -- a continuing resolution signed 2026-09-02 funds the government through 2026-12-11, so Sept payrolls (29k, 4.2% unemployment) printed on schedule Oct 2. Credit stress stayed concentrated in CCC-and-below HY (spreads near 12%, widest since late 2022) while IG spreads held tight. Oil firmed on Iran/Houthi tanker attacks near the Strait of Hormuz, keeping Brent above $100 despite higher Gulf export volumes. OCBC fell -5.90% on an Oct 7 Citi downgrade (NIM compression, valuation) and Energy Fuels fell -8.88% in a uranium/nuclear-sector-wide selloff with Oklo and Centrus Energy -- both now explained rather than flagged as anomalies. Hang Seng Tech remains nearly 40% off its Oct 2025 peak on AI-monetization-gap concerns.

macro.regime: Late-cycle hawkish repricing -- equities near highs but cracking under a yield shock
macro.narrative: The feared government shutdown was averted when a continuing resolution signed 2026-09-02 funded the government through 2026-12-11, so the data calendar (including Sept payrolls, 29k/4.2% unemployment, released on schedule Oct 2) is currently intact. The dominant driver instead is the Fed: minutes from the Sept 15-16 meeting (25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% under new Chair Kevin Warsh, 12-0, dot plot signaling one more 2026 hike) landed Oct 7-8 just as 10-year yields spiked to roughly 5.33-5.36%, a 24-year high, before easing slightly after a well-received 10-year auction. Sticky services-price pressure (ISM Services PMI 54.9, but the Prices sub-index at 74.0) is keeping the Fed hawkish even as jobs growth cools, a mildly stagflationary mix pushing the dollar to a two-month high (DXY ~102.2-102.4) and pressuring gold, silver and bitcoin (all down 1.3-2.8% on Oct 7). Credit stress is concentrated at the bottom of the quality curve -- CCC-and-lower HY spreads near 12%, widest since late 2022 -- while investment-grade spreads remain contained, suggesting idiosyncratic rather than systemic strain. Geopolitical risk is adding an oil premium: Iran/Houthi attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and on Saudi infrastructure are keeping Brent above $100 even as Gulf export volumes rise. In Asia, Hang Seng Tech has fallen almost 40% from its Oct 2025 peak on AI-monetization-gap worries even as BOJ Gov. Ueda's Oct 6 remarks reiterated a gradual hiking path.
